function.name: lawsuit_search
function.description: Search for lawsuits related to a particular subject matter in a certain location. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

location.description: The location to perform the search in.

subject.description: The subject matter of the lawsuits.

year.description: Optional. The year in which the lawsuit was filed. Default: 2024

message.content:
**Traffic Laws in Texas – Quick Reference Guide** | Topic | Key Points | Where to Find More | |-------|------------|--------------------| | **Speed Limits** | • Posted limits apply unless otherwise indicated.
• 55 mph on rural interstates, 65 mph on urban interstates.
• 45 mph on most rural highways, 35 mph on urban highways.
• School zones: 25 mph (or 20 mph if posted). | Texas Transportation Code §§ 545.001‑545.004 | | **Seat‑belt & Child Restraint** | • All occupants must wear seat belts.
• Children under 8 years or 4 ft 9 in must use a child safety seat.
• Back‑seat seats are mandatory for children under 13. | Texas Transportation Code § 545.021 | | **Cell‑phone Use** | • Hand‑held devices are prohibited while driving.
• Hands‑free devices are allowed. | Texas Transportation Code § 545.021 | | **Driving Under Influence (DUI)** | • Blood Alcohol Concentration (BAC) ≥ 0.08 % is illegal.
• Lower BAC limits for commercial drivers and drivers under 21.
• Penalties include fines, license suspension, and possible jail time. | Texas Transportation Code §§ 545.021‑545.023 | | **Right‑of‑Way** | • Yield to pedestrians at crosswalks.
• Stop at red lights and stop signs.
• “Stop‑and‑yield” rules for school buses. | Texas Transportation Code §§ 545.021‑545.023 | | **Headlights & Visibility** | • Headlights must be on from sunset to sunrise and during inclement weather.
• Fog lights may only be used when visibility is ≤ 200 ft. | Texas Transportation Code § 545.021 | | **Towing & Hitching** | • Towing vehicles must have a tow bar or hitch approved by the Texas Department of Motor Vehicles (TxDMV).
• Properly secured loads are required. | TxDMV towing regulations | | **Vehicle Registration & Inspection** | • Annual registration renewal required.
• Vehicle inspections are mandatory for certain vehicle types. | TxDMV website | | **Parking Regulations** | • No parking in front of fire hydrants, on sidewalks, or in designated no‑stop zones.
• Pay‑meter and parking‑meter rules vary by city. | Local city ordinances | | **School Bus Rules** | • Vehicles must stop for school buses with flashing red lights.
• Children must remain seated until the bus stops. | Texas Transportation Code § 545.021 | | **Special Provisions** | • Texas has specific rules for bicyclists, motorcyclists, and commercial vehicles.
• Certain counties have additional local ordinances. | TxDMV and local county codes | --- ### How to Stay Updated 1. **Texas Transportation Code** – The primary source for all state traffic laws. 2. **TxDMV Website** – Offers downloadable PDFs, updates, and FAQs. 3. **Local County Websites** – For county‑specific ordinances (e.g., Dallas County, Harris County). 4. **Legal Resources** – Texas Law Help, Texas A&M Law Review, or local bar associations for case law and interpretations. --- ### Quick Tips - **Always check the posted speed limit**; it can change at construction sites or school zones. - **Use hands‑free devices** if you need to talk while driving. - **Keep your vehicle’s registration and inspection stickers up to date** to avoid fines. - **Be mindful of local ordinances**—they can differ significantly between cities and counties. If you need more detailed information on a specific aspect (e.g., DUI penalties, commercial driver regulations, or local ordinances), let me know!
